name: We Promised One Thing. It Got Out of Hand.
why_it_works: Escalation is a ladder the viewer climbs with you: each step is a little more ridiculous, so they keep watching to see how far it goes. Snapping back to the tiny, real promise at the end is the release, and it makes the brand's actual promise memorable because it was the starting point of the joke.

hook.pattern: State a small, ordinary promise, then announce that it went too far.
examples: We promised {{small_promise}}. It got out of hand.
It started with {{small_promise}}. Then nobody stopped us.
Someone asked for {{small_promise}}. We overdid it.

variables.name: small_promise
variables.description: The small, real promise the brand makes, lowercase noun phrase (4 words or fewer, spoken)

variables.name: level_1
variables.description: Step one: reasonable (8 words or fewer, spoken; start with a capital letter)

variables.name: level_2
variables.description: Step two: a bit much (8 words or fewer, spoken; start with a capital letter)
variables.example: Then a drumline in the parking lot.

variables.name: level_3
variables.description: Step three: way too far (8 words or fewer, spoken; start with a capital letter)
variables.example: Then the drumline got its own drumline.

variables.name: callback_tag
variables.description: A deadpan callback to one escalation step (4 words or fewer)

variables.name: absurd_peak
variables.description: The peak: biggest harmless image (12 words or fewer, spoken)
variables.example: The noise registered on a weather app.

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What the viewer gets for acting

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine print for the client's niche, copied from the matching pack in compliance/packs.json
variables.example: Results vary. These statements have not been evaluated by the FDA.

beats.purpose: hook: the promise and the warning
beats.on_screen_text: We promised {{small_promise}}. It got out of hand.
beats.voiceover: We promised {{small_promise}}. It got out of hand.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of a calm, ordinary scene at {{brand}} with one small hint of chaos at the edge of frame, bright daylight, documentary style, centered subject
Vertical photo illustrating {{level_1}} at {{brand}}, cheerful and normal, warm light, a few people, eye-level framing

beats.purpose: escalation step two: a bit much

visual.prompt: Vertical photo illustrating {{level_2}}, noticeably bigger crowd or props, same location and color grade as before, energetic, slightly wider framing

beats.purpose: escalation step three: way too far

visual.prompt: Vertical photo illustrating {{level_3}}, comically oversized version of the previous scene, wide angle, dramatic light, playful chaos but safe

beats.purpose: peak: the absurd top of the ladder

visual.prompt: Vertical cinematic clip showing {{absurd_peak}} in a big, harmless, exaggerated way, camera slowly pulling back to reveal the scale, golden hour light, epic but goofy
Vertical medium shot of one {{brand}} person standing alone in the now-quiet location, straight face to camera, confetti on the ground, calm flat light

beats.voiceover: {{offer}}. We'll try to keep it reasonable.

cta: {{offer}}. We'll try to keep it reasonable. No promises.

craft.technique: Escalation ladder with a deadpan snap-back
craft.notes: Setup: one small, true promise, and the warning that it got out of hand, which tells the audience to expect a ladder. Escalation: four steps, each the same length and framing but bigger, from reasonable to a bit much to way too far to the absurd peak; the pace stays fixed so the size does the work. Turn: smash cut to silence and a single person delivering 'Anyway' straight to camera; the drop in scale is the laugh. Tag: a deadpan line that calls back to one escalation step (the callback_tag, e.g. 'Drumline not included.'). Timing: steps one to three are exactly 3 seconds each so the rhythm is a drumbeat; the peak gets 5 seconds to breathe; cut out the music on the frame before 'Anyway' and hold that silence for a half second.

do_not: Make any escalation step dangerous, illegal or something viewers would copy
Escalate at a rival team, artist or business; the ladder only climbs on the brand's own effort
Speed up the steps; the even rhythm is the joke
Forget to state the real promise again at the snap-back
compliance: Fitness trainers: no escalation step may show or promise a body, weight or performance result, and no step may involve unsafe exercise; results vary, and no step may read as a guarantee
Sports teams: no real league, rival team or player likeness without permission
Every escalation step must be safe and legal; nothing a viewer could copy that is dangerous
